speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) for each year since 2009, how many drivers have been fined under the Environmental Protection and Management (Vehicle Emissions) Regulations for leaving the engines of their stationary or parked motor vehicles idling; and (b) how effective has public education been in reminding drivers to adhere to this Regulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) adopts a multi-pronged approach to tackle pollution from idling vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA carries out public outreach to engage motorists on the importance of switching off their vehicle engines when stationary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA works with authorised vehicle inspection centres, vehicle fleet owners and schools to disseminate educational pamphlets to raise awareness of the regulations and promote compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Signs reminding motorists against idling engines are installed at hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We urge drivers to do their part to protect the health of others and reduce emissions by not leaving their engines idle when stationary.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is heartening to know that the numbers have dropped over the years, from 2009 to 2019, over a period of 10 years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, 2,800 is still quite a large number every year for enforcement acts to catch recalcitrants.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I am just wondering whether awareness of this regulation is included in our Highway Code before drivers actually get the licence to drive vehicles.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because, I am sure, for most of us here, we would sometimes come across stationary vehicles or parked vehicles and the engines are left idling.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For me, I have gone up to the person myself and told him, "You should turn off your engine while the vehicle is stationary".

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Beyond that, how can public education efforts be stepped up so that the numbers can be further reduced and that the awareness is there?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That is not just about protecting people's health but it is also being kinder to the environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The idea really is, as the Member has said, to enhance awareness as well as compliance right from the start.
